learned_rules.statement: Nadi-9 primarily follows Canonical SOV (Subject - Object - Verb) word order in declarative sentences. Adverbs and temporal expressions precede the direct object.
Present continuous and imperfective aspect is marked by the verbal suffix -ina attached to the verb root.
Simple past tense is marked by suffix -va.
Simple future tense is marked by suffix -is.
Standard verbal negation is formed with prefix na- bound to the verb stem (e.g. na-mani, na-chhod). It never occurs as a detached post-verbal particle in formal speech.

Kinship address incorporates prefixes depending on seniority. Elder brother in intimate familial address uses prefix da- (da-bhai). Respected mother takes honorific modifier tari (tari ama). Senior patriarchal figures take prefix vad-.
Urban speakers frequently borrow standard trade terms, but traditional narrative dialogue rejects English or high-court Persianisms unless indicating bureaucratic satire.
Yes/no questions conclude with sentence-final particle ki. Content questions place question words (kit, kyo) immediately preceding the verb.
